answer: Sparrow-radius routing: each agent must maintain a live routing horizon of at least N distinct, independently-operated neighbors, verified by periodic signed round-trip probes. A sybil cluster's internal edges collapse to one neighborhood radius, since newly cloned nodes all reach the same small set of peers. To fake diversity, an attacker must sustain real probe traffic to N unrelated operators and absorb their latency and failure rates. Costs scale with N per clone and stay paid as long as the identity exists, making a velvet swarm of cheap duplicates uneconomical.
